ui.universe.walk.dragScene: A drag moves the scene (not the look)
ui.universe.walk.credit: Ground: Terrain Tiles (USGS 3DEP, SRTM and GMTED2010; NOAA ETOPO1; national models; all credited on the Sources page); imagery as from orbit, with illustrative rock, soil and plants up close. The sea is drawn as water at sea level, its waves and glint illustrative (and, for now, so is land below sea level).

ui.universe.descent.hereVenus: Fall through Venus’s clouds to its ground where the Pioneer Venus Large Probe went in 1978, with what it measured on the way down.
ui.universe.descent.hereJupiter: Fall into Jupiter’s clouds where the Galileo probe went in 1995, with what it measured on the way down, until its signal stopped.
ui.universe.descent.label: Going down through the atmosphere
ui.universe.descent.probe: The readings are the {probe}’s, measured as it went down on {date} at {place}.
ui.universe.descent.cloud: {state}, as the probe’s nephelometer saw it
ui.universe.descent.wind: Wind {speed} m/s from the west, as the probe’s radio signal measured it
ui.universe.descent.between: Between the two probes’ readings here: interpolated.
ui.universe.descent.bottomVenus: The ground, where the Large Probe came down. Landing…
ui.universe.descent.bottomJupiter: The probe’s signal stopped here, at 22 bar: nothing below has been measured.
ui.universe.descent.keys: Falling as the probe fell · S faster · W climbs · drag or the arrows look round · Esc goes back to orbit
ui.universe.descent.touch: Drag to look round · hold Faster or Climb
ui.universe.descent.creditVenus: Readings: the Pioneer Venus Large and Day Probes (NASA, 1978), from the Planetary Data System; the haze from the Large Probe’s nephelometer; the colours and the light illustrative.
ui.universe.descent.creditJupiter: Readings: the Galileo probe’s atmosphere structure, nephelometer and Doppler wind experiments (NASA, 1995), from the Planetary Data System; the haze from its nephelometer; the colours and the light illustrative.
ui.universe.sound.label: Sound
ui.universe.sound.hint: Sound only where there is air to carry it: the wind on foot and on the way down through an atmosphere, the suit’s fans on a world without air. Space is silent.
ui.universe.stars.openHint: Out past the planets to the stars within 25 parsecs (82 light years), each where Hipparcos measured it, with the planets known around them.

ui.universe.walk.creditMars: Ground: the heights Mars Global Surveyor measured by laser (MOLA), about 7.4 km apart, with illustrative grain, craters and stones between them, credited on the Sources page; its colour as from orbit; the sky’s colour illustrative.

ui.universe.walk.creditMercury: Ground: the heights MESSENGER measured (USGS’s global elevation model), about 5.3 km apart, with illustrative grain, craters and stones between them, credited on the Sources page; its colour as from orbit.
ui.universe.walk.creditVenus: Ground: the heights Magellan measured by radar (USGS’s global topography), about 13 km apart, with Magellan’s gaps filled from around them and illustrative grain and stones between them, credited on the Sources page. Its colour, light and sky are illustrative: no Sun or star is seen under the clouds.
